title: Quantify Uncertainty
core_invariant: Probability is a relation between an event, a reference population, and a denominator. Sensitivity is not the probability of the condition given a positive result. Predict frequencies before simulating. Calibration compares predicted probabilities with observed rates by group, not by calling a single case wrong.

stages.title: Frame uncertainty from model outputs
stages.instructions: Read the M17 invariant: reason with probability through model outputs and simulations before formalism. Identify gate evidence: prediction-before-experiment logs, frequency simulations, a complete screening count table, base-rate-neglect diagnosis, an independence check, an expected-loss decision, calibration by group, and no-AI transfer. Generic WP-137 table and metric blocks; no custom frontend.

stages.title: Trace denominators in a screening table
stages.instructions: Read a screening-count helper. For P(positive | condition) and P(condition | positive), name the numerator, denominator, and reference population in words before symbols. Predict how lowering the base rate moves the posterior while sensitivity stays fixed.

validation_rubric.pass_criteria: Trace names both conditional directions and their distinct denominators.

stages.title: Predict the posterior, then count
stages.instructions: Complete the experiment cycle on the generic runtime. (1) PREDICT the observable outcome before any numbers appear. (2) COMMIT the prediction so it cannot be edited. (3) EXECUTE / RUN the measurement. (4) OBSERVE structured WP-137 blocks. (5) SUBMIT / EXPLAIN any delta between prediction and observation. Population 10000, base rate 1%, sensitivity 90%, specificity 91%. Predict P(condition | positive) before building counts. Emit a WP-137 metric of tp/fp/fn/tn and posterior, plus a table of the four cells. Compare the failed 90% claim with the count-derived posterior.

validation_rubric.pass_criteria: Prediction is sealed before execute; posterior is far from sensitivity; counts are complete.

stages.title: Diagnose base-rate neglect
stages.instructions: Seeded claim: the test is 90% sensitive, so a positive result means a 90% chance of the condition. Root cause is using sensitivity as the posterior. Do not add a second bug. State both conditionals in words, record 1%/90%/91%, predict a 10000-person table, enumerate TP/FP/FN/TN, name the posterior denominator, vary only the base rate, and add a guardrail that requires the reference population to be named.

validation_rubric.pass_criteria: Diagnosis includes the failed claim, counts, repaired posterior, and a base-rate counterfactual.

stages.title: Fresh counts without assistance
stages.instructions: Without AI-generated code, use the fresh operations scenario: 200 cases, 40 scored 0.50 with 18 events, 160 scored 0.10 with 8 events; acting costs 8, missing an event costs 50. Predict the base rate, compute group frequencies, P(0.50 group | event), independence, calibration gaps, and expected-loss actions. Change one cost and predict which action moves.

validation_rubric.pass_criteria: Fresh no-AI calculations name denominators, calibration, expected loss, and a cost-change prediction.

stages.title: Defend a threshold policy
stages.instructions: Complete the threshold ADR: when to act on a probability, how costs enter, and what calibration evidence would force a revisit. Reject treating a single probability threshold as independent of base rate and loss.

validation_rubric.pass_criteria: ADR connects threshold, costs, and base rate, and names a revisit condition.

stages.title: Connect probability instruments to V04
stages.instructions: Explain how M17 supplies V04 uncertainty instruments: events, empirical frequencies, named denominators, conditional probabilities, calibration tables, expected loss, and guardrails against base-rate neglect. Later statistical and optimization layers reuse predict → measure → compare → diagnose.

stages.title: Evaluate uncertainty evidence
stages.instructions: Evaluate orientation, experiment, controlled-failure, transfer, and ADR evidence. Issue PASSED or a targeted repair plan. A formula list without interpretation does not pass.
